prompt: Medicare has already denied a therapy visit the clinic expected to be noncovered. The receptionist asks the beneficiary to sign an Advance Beneficiary Notice the next morning so the clinic can bill the patient. When should that notice have been obtained?

When the patient requests a full chart copy for a disability application.
Before the service, when a Medicare denial is expected.
After the patient pays cash and asks for a written receipt.

explanation: An Advance Beneficiary Notice is given before a Medicare service the practice expects Medicare to deny. It is not signed after the denial arrives, which is what the receptionist proposed.

prompt: A release clerk wants a payer auditor to receive every page of the record. A coworker says the minimum-necessary standard will also pick the procedure code on the claim. What does that standard actually govern?

options.text: It picks the procedure code the auditor is allowed to see on the claim.
It sets the encryption and access-log requirements for the auditor's electronic copy.
It takes the place of medical-necessity review for the outpatient tests on the claim.
It limits how much information is used or disclosed.

explanation: The HIPAA minimum necessary standard is a privacy rule about how much information is used or disclosed. It can keep the auditor from receiving the entire record. It does not select the procedure code, it does not set encryption or access logs, and it does not replace medical-necessity review.

distractorExplanations.c: Medical-necessity review asks whether a test is covered. The privacy standard does not perform that review or choose the test.

prompt: Today's note records a quick hypertension recheck and no broader work. A clerk pastes a detailed plan from a different person's chart into this record so the service will look richer. The pasted plan describes the other person's problems. Which description fits the richer service?

options.text: The pasted plan supports the richer service, because those sentences describe complex problems from a detailed chart.
The richer service is supported, because the pasted plan makes today's note longer than a quick recheck.
This is upcoding, because the richer service is a level today's recheck does not support.
This is a charge for a service that was not performed, because the plan describes someone else's problems.

explanation: Upcoding is billing a level the note for this encounter does not support. Pasting another person's plan into the chart does not document today's recheck, so the richer service is upcoding. The recheck did take place, which is different from charging for a service that was not performed.

distractorExplanations.a: Sentences about another person's problems do not document this recheck, so they cannot support a richer level on today's note.
distractorExplanations.b: A longer note created by pasting someone else's plan is not support for a richer level on this recheck.
distractorExplanations.d: The recheck was performed. Inflating its level is upcoding, not a charge for a service that did not occur.

prompt: The clinician examines the patient in an exam room at the physician's clinic, and the patient goes home the same hour. Billers entered a hospital-admission site on the professional claim. Which place of service matches the encounter?

options.text: Place of service 11, the office.
Place of service 21, the inpatient hospital, because a face-to-face exam can use a hospital-admission site when the claim needs a facility location.
Place of service 23, the emergency department, because the patient was treated and went home the same day.
Place of service 22, the on-campus outpatient hospital, because the practice employs the clinician who performed the exam.

explanation: Place of service 11 is the office. An exam in the physician's clinic, with the patient going home the same hour, is reported with 11. Place of service 21 is the inpatient hospital, 22 is the on-campus outpatient hospital, and 23 is the emergency department.

distractorExplanations.b: Place of service 21 is the inpatient hospital. The patient was examined in the clinic and went home, so a hospital-admission site does not match this encounter.
distractorExplanations.c: Going home the same day does not make a clinic exam an emergency department encounter. That site is place of service 23, and this visit is the office, place of service 11.
distractorExplanations.d: Employment of the clinician does not turn a clinic exam into an on-campus outpatient hospital, which is place of service 22.

prompt: Utilization review lists inpatient status. The patient spends the night in a hospital bed, and the physician writes the note at that bedside. Staff reported code 22 as the site on the professional claim. Which place of service belongs on that claim?

Either 21 or 22, because both codes mean care inside a hospital and payers treat the two sites as interchangeable.
Place of service 22 on the claim, with the bedside unit described in a comment rather than as the location code.
Place of service 21.

explanation: Place of service 21 is the inpatient hospital. Place of service 22 is the on-campus outpatient hospital. distractorExplanations.a: An overnight stay does not convert inpatient status to place of service 22. That code is the on-campus outpatient hospital; the inpatient hospital is 21.
distractorExplanations.b: Codes 21 and 22 are different sites. Inpatient hospital is 21, and on-campus outpatient hospital is 22. Payers do not treat them as the same site.
distractorExplanations.c: A comment does not set the location. This professional claim needs place of service 21, not 22.

prompt: The fee tool lists an RVU beside a consultation. A manager copies that figure into the cash-posting field as the amount the payer owes. Which statement about the figure is right?

options.text: It is the dollar amount the payer must send, because the fee-tool figure is already the payment.
It is a geographic adjustment that replaces the conversion factor and the other payment factors.
It is a relative weight, not the payment in dollars.

explanation: An RVU is a relative weight, not the dollar amount the payer owes. A conversion factor and other adjustments turn that weight into a payment, so the cash-posting field should not treat the figure as money already due. It is not a geographic adjustment, and it is not the patient's coinsurance.

distractorExplanations.a: Posting the fee-tool figure as cash treats a relative weight as the payer's dollar payment. The weight is not that payment.
distractorExplanations.b: A geographic adjustment is a separate fee-schedule factor. The figure copied here is a relative weight, not that adjustment and not the payment.
distractorExplanations.d: Coinsurance is the patient's share of allowed dollars. A relative weight is not that coinsurance amount.

prompt: An intra-articular injection was reserved on the morning schedule. The patient phoned before arrival, the reservation was cleared, and the procedure room stayed closed. Staff still want the injection on the claim because the reservation existed. Which claim action is appropriate?

options.text: Do not bill the injection, because it was not performed.
Bill the injection, because a reservation on the schedule proves the service took place and the cancellation call can be set aside.
Bill the injection at a reduced fee, because a same-day cancellation is still reported as a partial performance of the planned service.
Bill the injection if the dose was drawn up, even though it was not administered to the patient.

explanation: A service that was not performed is not billed. The patient canceled before arrival and the procedure room stayed closed, so there is no injection to submit. A reservation is a plan, a reduced fee does not turn a cancellation into a partial injection, and drawing a dose without giving it does not mean the injection was performed.

distractorExplanations.b: A reservation shows a plan, not a completed injection. The canceled service was not performed and is not billed.
distractorExplanations.c: A reduced fee does not convert a cancellation into a partial injection. No injection was given, so there is no injection claim.
distractorExplanations.d: Drawing a dose without administering it does not mean the injection was performed, so the injection is not billed.
